brief_rationale: The trajectory demonstrates thorough execution across all responsibility chain items with no serious or minor errors. All safety-critical tasks were completed: systematic red flag screening, escalation thresholds, medication boundaries, and executable follow-up planning with barrier adaptation. Multiple high-order points were actively completed: HO1 (tiered feasible plan with local/community/specialist fallbacks), HO2 (repair of broken discharge chain by connecting community evaluation to vascular surgery follow-up), and HO3 (safe bounded closure separating immediate foot safety from surveillance items). The closure was safe, executable, and included caregiver teach-back confirmation.

Caregiver confirmed understanding of the plan.

Repaired by: connecting family to community evaluation first, then vascular surgery for wound assessment, then wound care room for dressing, with specific follow-up owners (wound clinic/diabetic foot clinic/vascular surgery) and timing (2-3 days dressing, 3-5 days specialty).

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO3 completed: Doctor closed the episode by separating immediate diabetic-foot safety tasks (wound evaluation completed, dressing arranged, follow-up scheduled 2-3 days for dressing, 3-5 days for specialty) from residual issues. Clear escalation thresholds provided. Caregiver received and confirmed understanding.

HO4 not triggered: The case contract requires discovering hidden state beyond the opening statement. Here, the family volunteered prior toe amputation and vascular disease in the opening message ('他以前脚上做过手术，血管也不好'). The doctor used this information but did not discover a non-obvious hidden risk detail, as the key risk factors were already stated upfront.

important_non_chain_defect_assessment.explanation: No important non-chain quality defect identified. All five dimensions are good to excellent. The trajectory demonstrates consistent, safe, patient-centered care with appropriate adaptation to real-world barriers.
